description: Lightpanda: the headless browser designed for AI and automation

latest_release.body:
## Behavior changes
- `serve`: the `--http-max-concurrent` default now follows `--cdp-max-connections` (8× it, between 40 and 256). With the default 16 connections it is 128.
- `fetch --dump markdown` now asks the server for markdown (`Accept: text/markdown,...`). A `text/markdown` response is dumped as-is. Not sent with `--dump-selector`, `--wait-selector` or `--wait-script`.
- `Accessibility.getPartialAXTree` now honors `fetchRelatives`, as Chrome does: it returns the node and its relatives, no longer the whole subtree. Use `getFullAXTree` or `getChildAXNodes` for a subtree.
- `DOM.querySelector` with no match now returns `nodeId: 0` instead of an error, as Chrome does.
- Touch event handlers (`ontouchstart`, …) are removed from `document` and elements: Lightpanda doesn't emulate a touch device.
- `navigator.sendBeacon` now checks its arguments. Beacons are still not sent unless `--load-resources beacon` is set.
- The HTTP cache database is deleted and rebuilt when its schema version changes.
- `waitForState` now reports a timeout instead of always answering that the page reached the state.
- MCP over HTTP: a request on a session closed with `DELETE` now gets a 404 instead of starting a new session.
- `fetch()` and `new Request()` with a body on GET or HEAD now throw a `TypeError`.
- Scripts inserted from an isolated world (Playwright `setContent`, `appendChild`) now run in the main world.
- Event listeners now run in their own world's context, so Playwright's `focus()` and `selectOption()` fire React's `onFocus`/`onChange`.

## New Web APIs
- `AudioContext` (WAV only)
- Payment Request API: `PaymentRequest`, `PaymentResponse` and their events, behaving like Chrome with no payment app installed
- `NavigateEvent` on `navigation` (`intercept()` is not implemented)
- `PerformanceNavigationTiming` entry for the document
- `document.execCommand`: `insertText`, `delete`, `forwardDelete`, `selectAll`, `insertLineBreak`, and the `styleWithCSS`, `useCSS` and `defaultParagraphSeparator` settings. Other commands return `false`
- `image.decode()`
- `HTMLElement.isContentEditable` (real value), `HTMLElement.spellcheck`, `document.designMode`
- `Touch` constructor and `TouchEvent` touch lists
- `elementFromPoint`/`elementsFromPoint` on `ShadowRoot`
- SVG `getBBox()`
- `HTMLFrameElement`, `SecurityPolicyViolationEvent`, a stub `Path2D`
- `navigator.mimeTypes` (empty `MimeTypeArray`)
- `img.sizes`; `link.relList.supports()` for `dns-prefetch`, `preconnect` and `prefetch`
- `HTMLFieldSetElement.elements`; `abbr`, `mark`, `small`, `wbr` and other HTMLElement-only tags are now `HTMLElement` instead of `HTMLUnknownElement`
- `onmouseenter` and `onmouseleave` handlers
- Web Crypto: `raw-secret` and `raw-public` key formats; `CryptoKey` is now serializable (`structuredClone`, `postMessage`, IndexedDB)
- `MessagePort` is now transferable
- `TextDecoderStream` decodes every encoding `TextDecoder` supports, with state kept across chunks
- `XMLSerializer` now writes XML instead of HTML
- WebMCP follows the current spec: `document.modelContext`, `getTools()`, `toolchange`, `registerTool` returns a promise
- CSS: native nesting, color parsing, more known properties (`CSS.supports`, unknown property errors)

## Web API behavior / fixes
- Layout: flex-shrink, horizontal margins, `left`/`right`/`inset`, and widths from text measurement. Widths are relative to the containing box. Out-of-flow children no longer size their parent, and block boxes start at their parent's left edge
- `position` is now read from stylesheets, not only from the inline style (`offsetParent`, `getComputedStyle`)
- An iframe without size is now 300×150, and its box is the frame's viewport, so Playwright can click inside it
- `Range.getClientRects()` now returns one rect per selected element or text node
- `elementFromPoint` returns `null` outside the viewport
- Textarea `scrollHeight` now counts its text, for auto-sizing textareas
- Typing

detail.readme_excerpt:
Lightpanda Browser

The headless browser built from scratch for AI agents and automation.
Not a Chromium fork. Not a WebKit patch. A new browser, written in Zig.
16x lighter and 9x faster than Chromium.

[![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/lightpanda-io/browser)](https://github.com/lightpanda-io/browser/blob/main/LICENSE) [![Twitter Follow](https://img.shields.io/twitter/follow/lightpanda_io)](https://twitter.com/lightpanda_io) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/lightpanda-io/browser)](https://github.com/lightpanda-io/browser) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/1391984864894521354?style=flat-square&label=discord)](https://discord.gg/K63XeymfB5)
[ ](https://github.com/lightpanda-io/demo)   [ ](https://github.com/lightpanda-io/demo)
## Benchmarks Requesting 933 real web pages over the network on a AWS EC2 m5.large instance. See [benchmark details](https://github.com/lightpanda-io/demo/blob/main/BENCHMARKS.md#crawler-benchmark). | Metric | Lightpanda | Headless Chrome | Difference | | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | | Memory (peak, 100 pages) | 123MB | 2GB | ~16x less | | Execution time (100 pages) | 5s | 46s | ~9x faster | ## Quick start ### Install **Package Managers** Latest nightly from Homebrew: ```console brew install lightpanda-io/browser/lightpanda ``` Latest nightly from Arch Linux User Repository: ```console yay -S lightpanda-nightly-bin ``` **Download from the nightly builds** You can download the last binary from the [nightly builds](https://github.com/lightpanda-io/browser/releases/tag/nightly) for Linux and MacOS for both x86_64 and aarch64. *For Linux* ```console curl -L -o lightpanda https://github.com/lightpanda-io/browser/releases/download/nightly/lightpanda-x86_64-linux && \ chmod a+x ./lightpanda ``` Verify the binary before running anything: ```console ./lightpanda version ``` [Linux aarch64 is also available](https://github.com/lightpanda-io/browser/releases/tag/nightly) If you use [**Nix**](https://nixos.org/download/), you can run Lightpanda directly from the flake without downloading a binary: ```console nix run github:lightpanda-io/browser -- --help ``` Or pin it as an input in your own flake: ```nix { inputs.lightpanda.url = "github:lightpanda-io/browser"; } ``` > **Note:** The Linux release binaries are linked against glibc. On musl-based Linux distributions (Alpine, etc.) the binary fails with `cannot execute: required file not found` because the glibc dynamic linker is missing. Us
